$comment: The pixel law, as data. This is brand/ASSET_MANIFEST.md §'The pixel law, in one table' in a form the build can enforce — the sizes here are transcribed from that table, not invented, and BRAND_SYSTEM §5.1 remains the authority. If the two ever disagree, the manifest wins and this file is the bug. Tilesets are NOT here: data/registries/tileset_manifest.json already owns their contract.

grid.note: TILE_SIZE. Every sprite size below is a whole multiple of it, except doors, which the manifest lists as a deliberate 88x96.

rules.$comment: The per-file rules from the same table. tools/check_assets.py measures what can be measured; the rest are review items.
rules.format: PNG, RGBA, transparent background. No baked background colour.
rules.no_antialiasing: Hard pixel edges only. If the generator softened the edges the asset is not usable — re-do it, do not sharpen it afterwards. Review item: no tool measures softness.
rules.author_at_1x: Never generate at 4x and downscale; it produces muddy edges. Review item: no tool measures this.
rules.outline: 1px outline in the world's ink_world on anything in the play layer; none on sky/far/mid.
rules.sheet_layout: Frames read left-to-right, top-to-bottom, no padding and no margin. A single horizontal strip is the preferred layout for new art; SpriteSheet also reads the square grids the shipped crow/coin/door sheets use, deriving columns from the sheet width.
rules.body_box: A class's `body` is the collider, and it must fit INSIDE the drawn silhouette in every frame - never the frame size. Measured by tools/check_assets.py.

body.why: The collider, in frame pixels, measured up from the frame's bottom edge - which `anchor: feet` puts on the ground contact line. It is NOT the frame: a 64px character frame carries clear margin above the head (this class asks for 2-3px and the shipped crow has 13-17), and a collider sized to the frame sticks out of the top of the drawing. That is what made ceilings feel wrong - the crow stopped a third of a tile below a platform it had visibly not touched. The shortest silhouette in the shipped walk cycle is 47px, so 46 sits inside the art in every frame; check_assets.py measures the art and fails if it ever isn't.
body.why_width: The collider is NARROWER than the drawing on purpose, and this number is a level-design constraint before it is an art one. It was 40 -- the measured width of the crow -- which is 1.25 TILES, and a tile is 32. So a one-tile hole in a platform was 8px narrower than the character meant to fall into it, and the crow simply stood on the hole with its box resting on both lips. Seven of those holes are authored across five levels (level_01 x=69 is the one a playtester photographed, with the crow hovering over open air between two grass ledges) and not one of them had ever been a hole. 24px is three quarters of a tile, so a one-tile gap is a real gap with 4px of ledge-catch either side, and the wingtips overhanging a ledge is the generous direction for a seven-year-old to be wrong in. tools/check_level_reachability.py now fails any gap this box could bridge, so the two numbers cannot drift apart again.

character.description: The player. SPRITE_SIZE, matching the shipped crow.
art_notes: Leave 2-3px of clear margin inside the frame left, right and top so the silhouette is never clipped.
Feet touch the bottom edge of the frame — that edge IS the ground contact line.
Every frame of a cycle registered to the same origin, or the character swims.

enemy.description: Ground enemies. Same footprint as the player so threat reads at a glance.
art_notes: Same margin and registration rules as `character`.
Readable silhouette at 1x — a child has to tell it apart from scenery instantly.

body.why: The INTERACT zone, in frame pixels, measured up from the frame's bottom edge - which `anchor: feet` puts on the ground contact line. An owl has no collider; the only shape it has is the one a child has to walk into, so this is it. It was a 96x96 box in Npc.tscn, three tiles by three, and encounters fire on proximity - so an owl reached out and started a maths problem from a tile and a half away, at a child who was running past. Sized to the owl instead: the art is drawn 44x53 inside its 64px frame, so this is the bird, and a child now has to walk up to it.

npc.description: Friendly characters the player interacts with (the owls).
art_notes: Friendly and unthreatening; this is who a 5-7 year old meets before doing maths.
Same margin and registration rules as `character`.

prop.description: World objects that stand on the ground (owl stations). Chain links are NOT props — see `attachment`.
art_notes: Bottom edge of the frame is where it meets the floor.

attachment.description: 32x32 objects drawn attached to another entity rather than standing on the floor — the chain links across an owl's perch. ASSET_MANIFEST lists these at 32x32 alongside coins, not with the 64x64 owl station.
art_notes: Centred on its attach point, not bottom-aligned.
ASSET_MANIFEST requires a link to stay countable at 22px in a row of three, which is the size npc.gd draws it at — so the silhouette has to survive being read small.
Authored at 32 and drawn at 22 is a 0.6875 downscale. The manifest asks for both; if the links ever look mushy, author at 22 rather than sharpening the 32.

door.description: Level exits. The manifest lists doors as their own size, not as props.
art_notes: Bottom edge of the frame meets the floor.
Symmetric horizontally unless the door is deliberately handed.

pickup.description: Coins and small collectibles. One tile, centred on its spawn point.
art_notes: Centred, not bottom-aligned — these float.
Coins keep the shipped silhouette and the gold ink in every world.

bonus_pickup.description: The three big coins hidden in every level. Two tiles across, centred on its spawn point, and deliberately NOT the size of a coin: a child has to tell one from an ordinary coin across a screen, because a coin goes into a lifetime purse and this is a third of a level's progress.
art_notes: Centred, not bottom-aligned — these float, like a coin.
It must read as a BIGGER, RARER coin rather than a different object. The reward it stands for is the currency the child already understands.
Nine frames on a 3x3 grid, the same layout as the coin sheet, so replacing it is a file copy with no registry change.
There is no second asset for the collected state. big_coin.gd builds that from this same art - darkened to a tint of itself and ringed in gold - so a replacement gets its ghost for free.

ui.description: HUD and maths-board icons. The manifest allows 32x32 or 16x16 and nothing between.
art_notes: Must stay legible at 1x on a phone; no detail finer than 2px.
A head crop, not a shrunk full body, when derived from a world sprite.

parallax.description: Background mountain ranges, three per world. One screen wide and 18 tiles tall, tiled horizontally by a ParallaxLayer.
art_notes: Transparent above the ridge line. The sky gradient shows through it, so a baked background colour would cover the sky the strip is supposed to sit in.
Bottom edge is the horizon - `feet`, like anything else that stands on a line.
Tileable on x: the ridge height at column 0 must equal the height one past the right edge, or the seam walks across the screen every time the strip repeats.
No outline. sprite_spec's outline rule already exempts sky/far/mid, and an ink line here would pull the range forward into the play layer.
